headline: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz within two days on conditions as the US weighs new strikes; Brent near $104. Russian bombs killed 26 in Zaporizhzhia on 2 Nov. Cyclone Murasu is due ashore in Andhra Pradesh. The VIX rose above 20.

situations.name: US–Iran war and Gulf energy shock
situations.summary: Iran offered on 2 Nov to reopen Hormuz within two days if the US lifts its blockade; no US reply. Mines and a projectile hit ships on 1 Nov. Brent near $104.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine war and NATO's flank
situations.summary: Russian bombs killed 26 at a Zaporizhzhia aid point on 2 Nov after 759 drones on 1 Nov cut power in 10 regions; Jersey airspace shut 30–31 Oct.

situations.name: Super El Niño
situations.summary: ONI +2.2: drought in Australia and East Africa, record warmth and weaker carbon sinks.

situations.name: Ebola outbreak, DR Congo
situations.summary: DR Congo reports more than 5,000 Ebola deaths and 10,300+ cases (2 Nov), with cases in Kenya and Nigeria; a WHO emergency (PHEIC) since May.

situations.name: Sudan war
situations.summary: Record drone attacks on civilians in October; the army rejects talks; famine confirmed in 2025.

situations.name: Cyclone Murasu
situations.summary: GDACS red alert; IMD expected landfall near Ongole, Andhra Pradesh overnight 2–3 Nov with winds of 100–110km/h; flights cancelled at Chennai.

situations.name: France: debt stress and protests
situations.summary: OAT–Bund spread about 159bp (30 Oct); hundreds of thousands protested with clashes on 31 Oct, as unrest also hit Germany.

situations.name: Energy shock feeding inflation
situations.summary: US CPI at 4.0% on the oil shock; a Bank of England rise is widely expected on 5 Nov; Egypt hiked on 29 Oct.

situations.name: Record Binance hack attributed to North Korea
situations.summary: About $6.3bn drained from Binance in late October; FBI blamed North Korea; Binance says 95% replaced and withdrawals restored in phases (2 Nov).

signals.name: US equity stress
signals.summary: VIX above 20 at a three-month high as tech sell-off extends; S&P 500 3.5% off its high
signals.state: The VIX rose about 10% on 2 Nov to around 21, a three-month high and above the 20 Watch line, as the sell-off in technology shares extended; the S&P 500 slipped 0.3% and the Nasdaq 0.7% while the Dow gained 0.6% (Investing.com). The S&P 500 is about 3.5% below its 52-week high. The 3 Nov midterms, 5 Nov Bank of England decision and 6 Nov payrolls fall this week.
signals.for_you: Share prices are swinging more than usual. Pension and investment values may move more around this week's elections and central bank decisions.
signals.rubric_hit: VIX 21.1 ≥ 20 Watch line; S&P drawdown 3.5% < 10%

Its heavy weighting to oil, gas and mining firms has cushioned it from the energy shock and the 30 Oct sell-off in US technology shares. The Bank of England decides on rates on 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: UK shares are near record levels. Pension funds with UK equity exposure have not seen a market fall of note.

signals.name: Crypto stress
signals.summary: Binance restoring withdrawals in phases after $6.3bn theft; Bitcoin 11% below its high
signals.state: Binance began phased restoration of withdrawals on 1 Nov after about $6.3bn was stolen in late October, which the FBI attributed to North Korea; on 2 Nov it said it had replaced about 95% of stolen assets and showed full reserves for ten major assets (Help Net Security). Bitcoin was near $76,700 on 2 Nov, 11% below its high, so the Watch status rests on the exchange's continuing stress.
signals.for_you: Binance customers may still face delays on some withdrawals. Any shortfall in reserves would matter most for those holding funds on the exchange.
signals.rubric_hit: Top-10 exchange under stress (Binance phased withdrawals) = Watch; BTC drawdown 11% < 25%

signals.name: Private credit stress
signals.value: Q3 exits 11.5% of NAV vs 5% caps
signals.summary: Big private credit funds still capping withdrawals, though Q3 requests eased
signals.state: In Q3, 19 non-traded BDCs received redemption requests worth $13.8bn, 11.5% of NAV, and met about 40%, leaving $8.2bn unmet (Stanger, 2 Oct). Blackstone's BCRED held repurchases to its 5% cap against requests of about $4.3bn, roughly 10% of shares. Requests eased from 12.7% in Q2, and Stanger said demand may have peaked.
signals.for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may not be able to withdraw all their money when they ask. Effects so far are confined to fund investors.
signals.rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions (BCRED at 5% cap) = Watch

signals.for_you: Higher US inflation keeps global interest rates elevated, which affects borrowing costs well beyond the US.

signals.summary: Euro-area GDP +0.4% in Q3, though France contracted; PMIs softening
signals.state: Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct showed euro-area GDP up 0.4% in Q3, though French output contracted. October flash PMIs (23 Oct) showed expansion weakening, and the ECB warned on 29 Oct that energy prices pose downside risks to growth. Final October PMIs are due from 2 Nov; neither stagnation nor a sub-50 composite is yet confirmed.
signals.for_you: Europe is still growing, but the energy shock is beginning to bite. A slowdown there would weigh on UK exports.

Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion.
signals.for_you: China is not currently a source of global shock, though weak domestic demand keeps it reliant on exports and trade relations.

signals.state: The Fed held at 3.75–4% on 28 Oct after a September hike, and the ECB held at 2.50% on 29 Oct, warning of upside inflation and downside growth risks. The Bank of England decides on 5 Nov with a rise widely expected, and Egypt raised rates on 29 Oct. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move had been made as of 2 Nov.
signals.for_you: Interest rates are more likely to rise than fall in the near term in the US and UK, which affects mortgages, loans and savings rates.

signals.name: Emerging-market stress
signals.summary: Pressure on oil importers such as Egypt, but no emerging-market crisis
signals.state: The Egyptian pound passed 56 per dollar at the central bank on 26 Oct, a record low, and Egypt unexpectedly raised rates by one point to 20% on 29 Oct, citing energy prices (Rio Times). Indonesia has repeatedly intervened for the rupiah this year. No major emerging economy has defaulted, imposed capital controls or lost more than 10% in a month as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Oil-importing emerging economies are under strain from the energy shock. People with ties to Egypt may see further moves in the exchange rate.

signals.for_you: Expect continued high petrol, diesel and heating-oil prices, with knock-on effects on transport costs and inflation.

signals.value: Hormuz largely shut; mines and attacks
signals.summary: Hormuz largely shut after mine and projectile strikes on 1 Nov; Iran offers two-day reopening on conditions
signals.state: Iran's IRGC said two tankers struck mines in Hormuz on 1 Nov, and UKMTO reported a vessel hit by an unknown projectile in the strait the same day (CBS). On 2 Nov Iran said it could reopen the strait within two days if the US ends its blockade of Iranian ports and meets other conditions; no US reply had been reported (Euronews). Drones hit at least seven cargo ships off Romania and Bulgaria in October.
signals.for_you: Shipping delays and higher freight and insurance costs feed through to fuel and goods prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state guidance.

No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed, so the Alert line is not crossed.
signals.for_you: Shortages of specialist materials can raise costs and delay electronics, vehicles and defence equipment.

signals.summary: Hormuz closure has stranded Gulf urea exports; prices up but below April peak
signals.state: No non-Iranian granular urea has cleared Hormuz since mid-October, and Argus counts at least 21 vessels with 919,000 tonnes of urea held in the Gulf, against normal exports of about 1Mt a month (28 Oct). Middle East urea was $447.50/t on 27 Oct, well below the April peak of about $780.
signals.for_you: Higher fertiliser costs tend to feed into food prices over the following seasons, hitting import-dependent farmers and poorer countries first.

signals.name: Nuclear plant safety
signals.summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on one power line as strikes on Ukraine's grid continue
signals.state: Zaporizhzhia lost its last off-site line on 20 Aug, its 26th such loss, and ran on diesel for about 18 days until an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire allowed repairs (ANS). It still depends on a single 330kV line while Russian strikes on Ukraine's grid continue (1 Nov). Trump has raised further bombing of Iranian nuclear sites (Al Jazeera, 1 Nov).
signals.for_you: No radiological release has been reported. Official guidance in an emergency would come from the IAEA and national authorities.
signals.rubric_hit: IAEA-reported loss of all off-site power (Aug–Sep); plant still on one line

signals.summary: No G20 government collapse or coup; US midterms on 3 Nov

signals.name: Civil unrest
signals.summary: Mass protests with clashes in France, Germany and Portugal on 31 Oct–1 Nov
signals.state: Hundreds of thousands protested across France on 31 Oct, a third weekend, with clashes in several cities (Japan Times). signals.for_you: If you are travelling to France, expect transport disruption on protest days and avoid demonstrations. Check FCDO travel advice for France.

signals.name: Humanitarian funding gap
signals.value: WFP Gaza aid cut for 500k (19 Oct)
signals.summary: Funding gaps force WFP ration cuts in Gaza and the West Bank
signals.state: WFP said on 19 Oct it would cut monthly food aid in Gaza from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people and halve family rations, after receiving less than half its usual Palestine funding in 2026; it needs $450m for six months. West Bank aid was halved in September (Al Jazeera).
signals.for_you: Funding shortfalls reduce aid in crisis zones. OCHA and ReliefWeb publish appeal details.

signals.summary: UK CPI 3.5% in September; Bank of England expected to raise rates on 5 Nov

signals.for_you: Mortgage rates are more likely to rise than fall in the coming months. Savings rates may also edge up.

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.summary: Forecasters see the January energy cap rising about 26–27%, above the 20% Alert line
signals.state: The Ofgem cap for October to December is £1,723 a year for a typical dual-fuel household. Uswitch's average of supplier forecasts (30 Oct) points to a 27% rise in January 2027, and other forecasts put the increase at about £442 a year, both above the 20% Alert line, driven by the wholesale gas surge. Ofgem announces the January cap by 25 Nov.
signals.for_you: Household energy bills are likely to rise sharply from 1 January. Ofgem and Citizens Advice publish guidance on support if you're struggling to pay.
